title: Backend Development Foundations — REST Task Tracker API
description: Assesses whether the candidate can design and implement a correct, well-structured REST API with proper HTTP semantics, input validation, and error handling.

task_prompt.text:
Build a small REST API for a 'task tracker' with the following endpoints:
- POST /tasks — create a task (fields: title, description, status, dueDate)
- GET /tasks — list all tasks, support ?status= filter
- GET /tasks/:id — get one task
- PATCH /tasks/:id — update a task's status or fields
- DELETE /tasks/:id — delete a task

Requirements:
- Use Node.js + Express, Python + FastAPI, or Python + Flask. Your choice.
- Validate input. Return correct HTTP status codes (200, 201, 400, 404).
- Handle errors gracefully — no stack traces leaked to clients.
- Use an in-memory store (array or dict) — no database needed.
- Include a short README inside a comment at the top: how to run, sample curl commands.

Paste your complete code below. Work at your own pace — time is not scored.

dimensions.name: API Correctness
dimensions.description: Does each endpoint work as specified (correct routes, HTTP methods, and response shapes)?

scoring_guide.25-30: All five endpoints implemented with correct HTTP methods. POST creates with all required fields. GET /tasks supports ?status= filter. GET /tasks/:id, PATCH, and DELETE all work correctly. Response shapes include expected fields.
scoring_guide.17-24: Four of five endpoints correct, or one has a minor issue (e.g., filter not implemented, or PATCH does a full replace instead of partial update).
scoring_guide.9-16: Two to three endpoints correct. POST and GET work but PATCH/DELETE are missing or broken.
scoring_guide.0-8: Fewer than two endpoints correct, or the API routes are entirely wrong.

dimensions.name: Input Validation & Error Handling
dimensions.description: Are inputs validated? Are errors returned gracefully without leaking internals?

scoring_guide.17-20: Missing required fields return 400 with a clear message. Non-existent IDs return 404. No stack traces in responses. Error messages are user-readable, not raw exception text.
scoring_guide.12-16: Most validation present but one gap: e.g., missing fields accepted silently, or 500 returned instead of 404 for a missing ID.
scoring_guide.6-11: Some error handling but notable gaps: no validation of required fields, or stack traces visible in error responses.
scoring_guide.0-5: No meaningful validation or error handling. Crashes or exposes stack traces.

dimensions.name: HTTP Status Code Accuracy
dimensions.description: Are the correct HTTP status codes used for each scenario?

scoring_guide.13-15: POST returns 201. Successful reads and updates return 200. Not found returns 404. Bad input returns 400. Delete returns 200 or 204. No 200 used where a more specific code is appropriate.
scoring_guide.8-12: Mostly correct but one or two wrong: e.g., POST returns 200 instead of 201, or delete returns 204 incorrectly.
scoring_guide.4-7: Status codes are approximate but wrong in several cases: 200 for everything, or 500 for validation errors.
scoring_guide.0-3: Status codes are arbitrary or entirely wrong.

dimensions.name: Code Quality
dimensions.description: Is the code readable, well-named, and structured logically?

scoring_guide.17-20: Clear variable and function names. Routes are logically organised. Helper functions used where appropriate. No duplicated logic. Framework idioms used correctly.
scoring_guide.12-16: Mostly readable but some issues: generic variable names (data, x, temp), or logic duplicated across routes.
scoring_guide.6-11: Functional but hard to read: long functions with no separation, poor naming, or anti-patterns for the chosen framework.
scoring_guide.0-5: Very difficult to follow due to naming, structure, or framework misuse.

dimensions.name: Documentation
dimensions.description: Is the README comment clear enough for someone to run the server and test it?

scoring_guide.13-15: README comment includes: how to install dependencies, how to start the server, and at least 3 sample curl commands covering different endpoints.
scoring_guide.8-12: README present but incomplete: missing install steps, or only one sample command.
scoring_guide.4-7: Minimal README: just a one-line start command with no install instructions or examples.
scoring_guide.0-3: No README comment, or comment is too vague to be useful.

weighting_note: Weights sum to 1.0. Overall score = sum(dimension.score / dimension.max_score * dimension.weight) * 100.

calibration_history.note: Initial rubric — not yet calibrated against human graders.
